definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 splits 'character' into four senses (4.26 a code value of a coded character set, 4.27 a graphic character in a screen item, 4.28 a COBOL character, 4.29 a single code value in storage); 2023 drops those entries but keeps each sense under its own term (§2023:3.7 alphanumeric character, national character, §2023:3.93 graphic character, §2023:3.37 COBOL character repertoire), so the drop is of a heading, not of a meaning. '31-character' counts alphanumeric character positions in storage (4.29/4.31); the same unit in 2023.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:8.8.1.1/8.8.1.3.1/8.8.1.3.6 (standard arithmetic, 32-digit standard intermediate) bear on a function only through §2002:15.3.1 (numeric and integer function results under standard arithmetic); EXCEPTION-STATUS is alphanumeric, so they do not apply. §2002:15 is 2023's 15.1 word for word and §2002:15.1 (types of functions) differs from §2023:15.2 only by its sentence that the number of character positions is specified in the function definition (2023 admits dynamic lengths); RV1 itself fixes the 31-character length (§2002:15.28.2 RV1).
